prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, in which small molecules recruit E3 ubiquitin ligases to remove chosen proteins, from the PROTAC concept to the cereblon mechanism of thalidomide-type glue degraders

statement.case_for: I keep B056 with Crews, Deshaies and Handa. After round 1, seven of eight members agree on the chemistry: recruitment of an E3 ligase into a ternary complex gives event-driven, catalytic removal of a chosen protein, reproduced independently for about twenty-five years. The remaining question is only the third seat, and I think each of the three names rests on a distinct, datable step. Crews and Deshaies supplied the concept and first proof of principle. Handa identified cereblon as the target of thalidomide, which explains an old drug class and anchors the glue strand and most CRBN-recruiting degraders in the clinic. The chair asks whether one citation can cover PROTACs and glues without naming everyone. I think it can if it is worded around induced proximity to E3 ligases, which is how I have written mine, and that is more defensible with Handa than with a PROTAC-only trio, which leaves the most clinically consequential mechanism unrecognised.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation remains attribution and timing. Ciulli's VHL ligands and cooperativity work, Sakamoto's co-authorship of the 2001 paper, and Ito's role beside Handa on cereblon all have real claims that a three-person limit cannot honour. PROTAC and glue histories began separately, so a unified citation could be read as a compromise. No degrader is yet a broadly approved therapy, so part of the impact case is still prospective, which is why I want the citation to rest on the mechanism and not on clinical outcomes.

responses.point: Linke prefers Ciulli as third laureate because PROTAC design is a transferable principle and Ciulli's VHL ligands and cooperativity generalised it, whereas cereblon explains one family of molecules.
responses.response: This is the strongest argument for the other trio and I have weighed it again. I still come out with Handa for two reasons. Cereblon is not one family in practice: it is the E3 ligase behind most degraders now in the clinic, and it also explains thalidomide, lenalidomide and pomalidomide, so its reach is wider than 'one family'. And a citation built on 'induced proximity to ubiquitin ligases', which Linke himself says he could adopt, is only complete if the glue strand has a named origin. My answer to the chair's question is that I would accept Ciulli only if the committee deliberately chooses a PROTAC-centred citation, and I would then ask that the citation drop the glue wording, since a Ciulli trio would otherwise claim a strand it does not name.

responses.point: Sparr argues that the ternary-complex and VHL-ligand work gives PROTACs their quantitative, design-level physical chemistry, and that waiting for an approved degrader would hold the prize hostage to regulatory events.
responses.response: I agree with her on maturity and have moved on it: twenty-five years of independent reproduction of the mechanism is the right yardstick, and I do not want approval status to decide this. I also accept that cooperativity is the most physical-chemical part of the field. But that is the contribution that refines the concept, whereas the question of how cereblon works is what let the community understand why thalidomide-type drugs act at all. Her own file says Handa would be acceptable to her. Given that, the committee can reach five on a single trio, and I would ask her whether the cooperativity work could be recognised in the citation text or the scientific background, not in a named seat.

responses.point: Brzezinski supports Handa as the third name because each seat rests on a distinct, datable discovery, and asks that the citation be worded around the chemical and mechanistic principle, not therapeutic outcomes. He also wants the expert report to state how much of the ternary-complex framework is Ciulli's and not Crews's.
responses.response: I accept his correction on maturity and have reworded my case accordingly: the mechanism is settled, the clinical consequence is not, and the citation says nothing about approved therapies. I agree that the expert report should separate Ciulli's VHL-ligand and cooperativity contribution from the Crews laboratory's own VHL work, because that would settle whether Ciulli has a founding claim or a refining one. If the report shows that the framework is substantially Ciulli's alone, I would reconsider the third seat; on what is in front of me it does not.

responses.point: Chabes supports Crews, Deshaies and Handa and would accept Ciulli only for a PROTAC-centred citation, but notes the credit split among PROTAC inventors, cereblon discoverers and ligand developers is unresolved.
responses.response: We agree on the configuration. The chair's synthesis says we would both resist splitting B056 into separate PROTAC and glue parts, and I keep that position, with one refinement. A two-part split would cost the third seat and two names, and it would also separate two strands that share one mechanism, so I would use it only if no unified citation can reach five votes. I would also use Chabes' point on the unresolved credit to say that Sakamoto, Ito, Gray and Kim should be acknowledged in the scientific background and not displace any of the three names.

uncertainties: Whether the committee settles on Handa or Ciulli, and whether five votes can be reached on one trio; I could accept Ciulli with a PROTAC-centred citation.
How much of the VHL-ligand and ternary-complex framework is Ciulli's alone and how much came from the Crews laboratory; I would want the expert report to say.
Whether the absence of a broadly approved degrader makes recognition premature for some members; I think the mechanism is mature even though the clinical outcome is not.
I have not verified the chronology of the earliest PROTAC and cereblon reports or current clinical-trial status.
statement.conflict_note: No change since round 1. None of the credited names on B056 is a postdoc mentor (Stevens, Boey) or a Linköping colleague. My research overlaps scientifically with Emma Sparr's, which is not a personal or institutional connection to any shortlisted candidate.
